summary: A practical lesson on using the present perfect to discuss life experiences.
learning_objectives: Distinguish finished past events from unspecified life experiences.
Form present-perfect questions and short answers.

sections.title: Concept introduction
sections.summary: The teacher contrasts the simple past with the present perfect.
sections.visual_context: A slide shows have or has followed by a past participle.

sections.title: Guided speaking practice
sections.summary: Students ask and answer questions about experiences.
sections.visual_context: Conversation prompts are visible on the shared screen.

key_concepts.explanation: The present perfect connects a past experience to the present without naming a finished time.

vocabulary.meaning: Something that has happened to or been done by a person.
vocabulary.example: Travel can be a valuable experience.

grammar.explanation: Use have or has plus the past participle.
examples: Have you ever flown in a helicopter?

pronunciation.guidance: Practise the reduced forms in I've and she's.

teacher_corrections.explanation: Gone is the past participle of go.

student_difficulties: Choosing between the simple past and present perfect.

visual_materials.description: A grammar slide displays subject, auxiliary, and past-participle columns.
visual_materials.relevance: It reinforces the sentence structure explained in the audio.

suggested_exercises.instruction: Write five Have you ever questions and interview a partner.
suggested_exercises.answer_or_key: Answers vary; each question should use have plus a past participle.

next_steps: Contrast ever and never with already and yet.
transcript:
[00:00:00 - 00:00:05] Today we're going to talk about life experiences.
[00:00:05 - 00:00:10] Have you ever visited another country?
